title: Article archive: durable full-text storage for AI news
owner_goal: Keep the full text of every collected AI article permanently (source pages disappear), so the corpus can later support deeper analytics, RAG and Q&A. Raw material first, interpretation later.
depends_on: 006-daily-ai-signals should merge first (it adds durable mention evidence; the archive must not conflict with it)

facts_2026_10_18.monthly_volume: Oct 2026: 2622 articles (1451 with full text); Sep: 995 (324); Aug: 1520 (431)
facts_2026_10_18.growth_estimate: ~100 kept articles/day x ~10 KB clean text = ~1 MB/day, ~400 MB/year; raw HTML would be ~10 GB/year
facts_2026_10_18.deletion_paths: ArticleRepo.prune_older_than (retention 800 days, runs on deploy) and non-news cleanup delete article rows and their text
facts_2026_10_18.full_text_sources_today: RSS content when present; settings.rss_extract_full_text defaults to False (verify prod value); daily-publish downloads source pages into data/daily-enrichment/source-cache/pages/<key>/ (page.html, text.txt, evidence.json) but only for articles it needs (56 pages cached)
facts_2026_10_18.backups: scripts/db_backup.sh writes postgres_*.sql.gz to /opt/ai-news/backups on the same server, keeps 14 days, no off-site copy; the scheduler of the daily backup is not in crontab or the ai-news systemd timers (to verify)

principles: Never lose collected text: the archive is append-only and is not touched by retention prune or non-news cleanup (only by an explicit operator purge).
Store clean extracted text plus metadata and hashes; do not store raw HTML long-term by default.
Keep raw text first; condensed or interpreted forms are derived, versioned and re-computable from raw.
Internal analysis only: never republish full third-party text publicly; outputs use own conclusions, short quotes and links.
Small, testable steps; each step is a separate spec/PR following AGENTS.md.

tasks.title: Off-site backups before anything else
tasks.why: Backups live on the same VPS; losing the server loses all history. The archive makes the data the main asset.
steps: Find what actually schedules scripts/db_backup.sh on the server (cron, workflow, deploy hook) and document it.
Choose an off-site target (S3-compatible such as Backblaze B2 / Cloudflare R2, or a pull to the owner's Mac) and estimate cost.
Add encrypted upload after each backup, with its own retention (e.g. daily 30, monthly 12).
Run and document a restore test from the off-site copy.
tasks.done_when: A fresh backup exists off-site daily and a restore from it was tested.

tasks.title: Design where and how to store the archive
questions: Separate table (e.g. article_archive) in the same PostgreSQL vs compressed files (JSONL/Parquet by day) vs both (DB for recent, files for cold storage)?
Key and identity: url_canonical_hash plus content hash; how to handle updated articles (keep versions?) and duplicates across sources (ArticleAlias).

Fields: url, canonical url, source/publisher, title, author if known, published_at, fetched_at, language, clean text, text length, extraction method and version, content hash, http status, license/paywall flags.
Relation to articles table: no FK (must survive prune), same pattern as signal_mentions in 006.
Compression and size budget (text only ~400 MB/year); when to move old years to cold files.
Access control: archive is never exposed by public APIs.
Is raw HTML kept at all? Proposal: keep only for a short window (e.g. 30 days) to allow re-extraction, then drop.
tasks.deliverable: Spec in specs/ with data model, migration, retention and purge rules.

tasks.title: Backfill full text for articles that only have an RSS summary
questions: Which articles qualify: all stored, or only admitted/digest articles (cheaper, less noise)? Proposal: admitted articles first, oldest digest days last.
Reuse the existing downloader and extractor (storage/article_evidence_cache.py SourcePageDownloader, PageCache, text.txt) instead of a new fetcher.
Politeness: per-domain rate limits, robots.txt, user agent, retries, timeouts, total runtime caps; run outside the 01:00-03:00 UTC job window and under the host lock.
Failures: paywalls, 404 (page gone), JS-only pages, consent walls; record a status per URL and do not retry forever.
Quality check: minimum length, boilerplate ratio, language detection; sample review of extraction quality per source.
Measure: how many of the ~4000 articles without full text can still be fetched (pages already disappear).
tasks.deliverable: Resumable CLI backfill command with caps, a per-source success report and a sample quality review.

tasks.title: Collect full text every day going forward
questions: Where in the pipeline: at fetch time (rss_extract_full_text / HTML parsers), as a separate step after fetch, or reuse the pages daily-publish already downloads? Proposal: separate step after fetch for admitted articles, reusing the publish cache when available.
Ordering with daily-publish and daily-signals inside the existing daily job budget (TimeoutStartSec 14400) and host lock.
Failure isolation: archiving must never block or fail fetch, digest or signals.
Monitoring: daily counts (archived, failed by reason, coverage %) in the job log and on the admin stats page.
tasks.deliverable: Daily archive step with coverage metrics; target >= 90% of admitted articles archived with full text.

tasks.title: Decide on cleaning and condensing text (remove filler or not)
tasks.recommendation: Start with raw clean text only (boilerplate removed: navigation, ads, cookie banners, related links). Do not summarize or remove 'water' at storage time: what looks like filler today may matter for future questions, and condensing is lossy and model-dependent.
questions: Boilerplate removal level at extraction (deterministic, cheap) vs LLM condensation (paid, lossy).
If condensed forms are added later: store them as separate derived fields with model and prompt version (e.g. key facts list, entities, numbers, claims with quotes), recomputable from raw.
Chunking strategy for later RAG (by paragraph/section, overlap) is a derived step, not a storage format.
tasks.deliverable: Short decision record; no condensation in the first release.

tasks.title: Decide what else to capture with each article
candidates: Images: only URLs and alt text (no binary storage).
Outbound links in the article (sources, papers, repos) for citation graphs.
Numbers and facts mentioned (prices, benchmarks, funding amounts) as later derived extraction.
Author/byline, section/tags from the source, word count, reading time.
Social/discussion signals (HN, Reddit) as a separate future source.
Paper/repo metadata for research items (arXiv id, GitHub repo, Hugging Face model id).
tasks.deliverable: Prioritized list; each accepted item becomes a field or a derived table in A1's spec.

tasks.title: RAG / Q&A over the archive (later)
notes: Only after A1-A3 run for a while and concrete questions exist.
Likely PostgreSQL + pgvector; embeddings per chunk; small VPS (1.9 GB RAM) may need half-precision vectors or a separate host.
Answers must cite archived articles; internal use first.
Reuse 006 entities and events as filters (entity, event type, date range).

tasks.title: Legal and policy check
steps: Confirm storage for internal analysis is acceptable per source terms; respect robots.txt and opt-outs.
Document that full text is never republished; public outputs use summaries, short quotes and links.
Purge path for a source or URL on request.

order_rationale: Protect existing data first (A0); design storage (A1); start daily capture so no new text is lost (A3); then backfill what is still fetchable (A2); decisions on cleaning and extra fields (A4, A5) refine the design; RAG last.
